title: Affine evaluation of a quasi-coherent module colimit
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a small category, $F:I\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ a diagram of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $c$ a colimit cocone on $F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Assume every $F_i$ and the cocone point $c.\mathrm{pt}$ are quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For every affine open $U\subseteq X$, evaluation of $c$ on $U$ is a colimit cocone of $\mathcal O_X(U)$-modules.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID; Section 01LA, items (3)-(5). Local source read at /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/schemes.tex, lines 1435-1455 and 4717-4744.

proof.text: Restrict the diagram and cocone to Spec R, R = Γ(X,U), using the affine open immersion with image U. Restriction preserves colimits and quasi-coherence, and its sections identify with sections over U.

The restricted objects, including the cocone point, are quasi-coherent. Lift the diagram and cocone into the full subcategory of quasi-coherent modules. Full faithfulness of the inclusion reflects its colimit property. The inverse of tildeEquiv is the global sections functor on this subcategory and preserves colimits. This proves the global-section cocone on Spec R is colimiting.

For each module the restriction section isomorphism at top, followed by the restriction isomorphism along the equality image(top)=U, identifies the section modules. Linearity follows from fromSpec.appIso and ΓSpecIso, which carry r to the restriction of r. Naturality of restriction on module morphisms identifies each evaluated cocone leg. Transport the colimit across this natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Explication of Stacks 01ID and 01LA using the existing Lean tilde adjunction and affine cover.
